items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: No, I'd have, I always took a tenor with me. I took a tenor. Most of the time it was Buddy Tate because Buddy and I had made so many records together.

ctx.x: Now when you went to Toronto and London House what sort of group would you have as a rule. A rhythm section and trumpet or would you have another horn?
No, I'd have, I always took a tenor with me. I took a tenor. Most of the time it was Buddy Tate because Buddy and I had made so many records together. You know, Buck and Buddy, Buck and Buddy Blues.
At the London House I went out there with Ja Jones, when he had a trio. of..

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Yeah. Freddie, Earl, Jack Washington, Buck, Sweets, Dickie Well, Shad Collins was playing his ass off.

ctx.x: Was Freddie Green with the band then?
Yeah. Freddie, Earl, Jack Washington, Buck, Sweets, Dickie Well, Shad Collins was playing his ass off.

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And maybe four or five trombones. There’s Sweets and Buck. Vic Dickenson, Dan Minor.

ctx.x: What size was the band at that time? Who was —

Well, we got about one, two, three, got five saxes. One, two three. Let’s see Prez, Jack, yeah, there’s five saxes. One, two, three, four, five. Five saxophones. And maybe four or five trombones. There’s Sweets and Buck. Vic Dickenson, Dan Minor.
It seems to me that the players at that time were not only good players, but real personalities.
